At first I was like "yeah, that was awesome!" But by the time I got to my car and sat down, I really started to think less of it. Now it's my least favorite of the films. It was just a complete rehash of Episode IV. The whole thing was a circlejerk for the classic trilogy purists. If you judge it on its own, it was an all right movie, but that's the thing. Nobody judges it on its own because it's part of a series. Judging it that way, there's nothing original about it.

I also want to talk about the EU, or rather, the lack thereof. This film added no substantial amount of lore to the galaxy. If you're going to scrap the old EU, at least create a new one. This film felt so small in comparison to the other films. It felt more like a brainless action film and less like a chapter in an epic saga with a rich back story. Growing up, I liked Star Wars, but I didn't love it as much as other people. It wasn't until I discovered the EU and learned of the galaxy's long history, all its cultures, all the long-gone nations, etc. that I really enjoyed it. I love worldbuilding, so franchises that really show that off are much more interesting to me than ones that don't have any detailed lore.

This is where I want to talk about the prequels. Say what you will about them, but they had a lot of lore and a huge scope. A lot of people say the dialogue sucked, especially when it came to Anakin, but I disagree. Moviegoers would say that people don't naturally talk like they do in the prequels. Once again, I disagree. Anakin talks pretty much exactly like I do. My voice is very monotonous, and even when I'm angry, I talk as if I'm debating or as if I have to tell people what I'm feeling in the moment. Episode II came out when I was around 15, and after we watched it, my parents commented that in the scene where Anakin made the "I slaughtered them like animals" speech to Padme, that his word choices and emotions looked a lot like me when I would become angered. So yeah, not seeing the "bad dialogue" gripe.

As for all the political stuff (senate hearings, talking about taxation of trade routes, etc.) people comment that it's not interesting or fun for a sci-fi/fantasy action film, but I disagree. I love political intrigue, and this made the films more intelligent and added to the lore. Maybe I'm biased, as I have a degree in political science, but I really didn't see a problem with this. There's stuff like this in things like Game of Thrones and nobody seems to care, so why should they in the prequels?

As for the plot holes, yes, there are a few, but there have been plot holes since the beginning. What do you expect of a series that was made up as it went along? Vader was never supposed to be Anakin. Leia was never supposed to be a Skywalker. The list goes on.

In short, TFA was not Star Wars and even the prequels, regarded as the least good of the films, were tons better.
